03_economic_journal.notes: Two parts. (1) signal-copier/app/economics.py: fixed the completed_trade_win_rate naming issue flagged in Phase 00 -- renamed the existing (genuinely fill-based) metric to closing_fill_win_rate, kept completed_trade_win_rate as a deprecated alias (same value, so nothing calling it breaks), and added a real completed_lifecycle_win_rate that counts independently completed position episodes (flat -> non-flat -> flat), with break-even episodes tracked separately from wins/losses. A position closed across several partial-exit fills is one episode, not one-per-fill -- the two metrics can disagree (tested) exactly when a losing partial exit is offset by a winning one in the same episode. 928 signal-copier tests pass (12 new). (2) signal-portfolio-commercial/app/models/ledger.py + app/services/ledger.py: the four-book (source/model/platform/follower) append-only economic journal itself -- Numeric/Decimal money fields (never Float), a real Postgres BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger (app/db.py's enforce_append_only) that rejects direct mutation even for the table owner, and append_correction() that fixes a mistake by inserting a new row referencing the original via correction_of, never editing it. This is deliberately NOT a wrapper around app/provider_value.py -- it's a new, generic, multi-book ledger; provider_value.py remains what it was, a narrower single-owner analysis tool. 6 new tests (41 total in this package). ruff/mypy clean both places.

06_collective2_publisher.notes: app/services/collective2_publisher.py builds (never sends) the API4 Order envelope from a PublicationIntent. The TIF resolution this build was asked to do first was ATTEMPTED and BLOCKED, not guessed: this session tried WebFetch on https://collective2.com/apidoc/v4 to resolve the spec's own flagged conflict (docs documenting TIF0=day/1=GTC but one conditional example using 2) and the request was refused by this environment's egress policy (collective2.com is not an allowed domain), confirmed via /root/.ccr/README.md as an organization policy denial, not a transient failure -- per that file's own instruction, such denials are reported, never retried or routed around. Consequently `Tif` defines ONLY the two undisputed values (DAY=0, GTC=1); the disputed value 2 is not a member and build_order raises UnsupportedTifError defensively if a TIF outside those two is ever produced. Every issued intent currently resolves to DAY (the more conservative of the two undisputed values) via a single `_resolve_tif` function, pending a real per-portfolio TIF policy. Also implements: OPEN/ADD map to a BUY market order, REDUCE to a SELL market order (quantity_basis must be UNITS, an integer whole number, or the build refuses rather than truncating/rounding); STOP_UPDATE/TARGET_UPSERT map to a PriceOnlyModification envelope per docs/06's 'price-only modifications, not general direction/duration/quantity replacement'; CLOSE/ENTRY_CANCEL/STATUS_CORRECTION/STRATEGY_PAUSE/TARGET_REMOVE/TARGET_CLEAR have no mapping yet and raise rather than guessing. 13 new tests (83 total). Load-bearing verification: broke the REDUCE-is-SELL mapping and the fractional-quantity rejection in turn, confirmed the matching tests failed, restored exactly. ruff/mypy clean.
06_collective2_publisher.not_yet_wired: No transport -- nothing calls the real API4 HTTP endpoint (no credentials exist in this environment; CARD-3 platform agreements and a real scoped API4 Bearer key are prerequisites, not yet obtained). No StrategyId/instrument-approval resolution, no C2Symbol/ExchangeSymbol lookup (c2_symbol is passed in by the caller, not resolved here), no OCA/stop-target group reconciliation, no external-acknowledgment readback wired to publication.transition(). Remains BLOCKED for the TIF=2 question specifically -- do not widen the Tif enum without real, captured vendor confirmation, and do not attempt collective2.com again from this environment without the egress policy changing.

10_pamm_mam_domain_model.notes: Simulation only, per docs/07: 'Production uses the actual contractual broker rule instead.' app/services/mam_allocation.py implements the largest-remainder (Hare quota) integer-unit allocation with deterministic account-ID-ascending tie-break and per-account caps -- every rounding remainder is recorded for audit, total allocated + unallocated always equals the input exactly, and an unallocatable remainder (every account already at cap) is explicit, never silently dropped or forced past a cap. app/services/pamm_accounting.py implements the simple test-only no-cashflow-interval high-water-mark fee exactly as specified (fee = positive part of (pre-fee NAV - previous HWM) x rate; new HWM = max(previous HWM, post-fee NAV); losses carry forward, never charging a negative fee) and REJECTS any interval flagged as having a deposit/withdrawal rather than computing a wrong fee for it, plus a deposit/withdrawal-to-units conversion at a dealing NAV that refuses a non-positive price. 17 new tests (154 total). 11_llm_assistance.notes: app/services/model_gateway.py builds the capability/permission boundary docs/11 requires, mirroring app/services/permissions.py's explicit allow-list pattern from Phase 02. No model provider API key exists in this environment and none is needed for this module -- the boundary IS the deliverable. ModelPurpose is the spec's own closed 'allowed candidates' list (tag proposals, parser-rule drafts, frozen-report summaries, method explanations, support triage, product-copy drafts, offline classification comparison). require_model_permitted_action() enforces the spec's own 'Disallowed' list as a hard, unconfigurable deny-list with no bypass parameter anywhere -- inventing signal parameters/history/APIs, deciding rights/jurisdiction eligibility, approving marketing, changing portfolio weights/risk, placing/canceling orders, granting entitlements/permissions, altering HWM/NAV/fees, cross-tenant reads, evaluating with customer API keys, recommending a personalized portfolio (covers the support-triage caveat too), approving its own production changes, and auto-publishing output are all always rejected regardless of purpose or configuration. requires_human_review() is unconditionally True for every purpose ('Model-generated content cannot be automatically published'). build_model_gateway_config() validates the typed gateway config docs/11 requires (purpose/version/max input-output/budget/tenant scope/data-use agreement) and refuses anything missing or non-positive rather than defaulting to unlimited/unscoped. validate_api_key_role() enforces 'Provider API keys are read-only research role secrets, not trading keys.' 34 new tests (188 total). Load-bearing verification: removed one disallowed action from the deny-list and disabled the API-key-role check in turn, confirmed the matching tests failed, restored exactly. ruff/mypy clean.

standing_constraints: Never place live orders or rotate live credentials.

No investment deposits through SaaS billing or improvised pooled wallets.
LLMs are optional reviewed aids only -- no rights, risk, fee, NAV, publishing, cross-tenant, or self-approval authority.
Missing drivers/credentials remain BLOCKED/NOT_RUN, never PASS.
Never paste passwords, customer documents, platform keys, or signed contracts into source control.
signal-copier/ (existing execution service) stays untouched by this build; separate Postgres database, never the owner's SQLite store or broker credentials.
Every test suite run must pass, and every load-bearing fix must be verified by temporarily breaking it and confirming a test catches the regression.
